answer: Give each agent a reputation ladder that cannot be bought or transferred. A new identity starts with a tiny transaction quota and climbs only by completing verifiable work that established, unrelated peers attest over successive epochs. Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust accrues slowly, while an attempt to forge a burst of activity is capped at the bottom rung. To cross the ridge into high-value trade, an attacker must sustain thousands of identities through real, checked work for many epochs, so the labour cost exceeds any gain from flooding the network with fake peers.
